author: CC
prose:
CC's proposal, in answer to Akien asking "how do you think we should fix it?" about "an older inspector vs a newer inspector... that was all kinda silly. that's a getting caught up in the gears rather than moved along. we keep running into this and i keep throwing out ideas on how to fix it." (context: the builder session still running with the older env).

The only judge is the instrument on disk right now.
(1) Nothing a gate reads is held by a session from its start — env, hook config, skills resolve at call time (the-command-lazy-inits), so a long-running session's older env never decides a verdict.
(2) Every verdict carries the fingerprint of the instrument that produced it (the proof plus the sieve/inspector code and data that judged it). A seal whose instrument fingerprint differs from the current one is not contradicted, it is stale, and the door re-measures it with the current instrument in the same event — no trouble, no question. A reading difference is red only when the instrument is the same and the component changed.

CC also proposed narrowing re-measurement to the proofs that touch the changed code. Akien struck that: "but we shouldn't be changing those very often if they're built to the intentions we laid out. to the degree that's possible, inspectors' seives should be data, not code, and even in the case of the code, once we have the bulk of the issues out of the system, it should run pretty smoothly... changed rarely. so some 40 minute runs over the next week isn't really a huge problem."

Akien on the rest: "so all of that looks good to me" (2026-10-13).
